W3's own reading of the same observation (M3) is left standing beside this one and is not mentioned.

findings.forced_edit: Strike the difference half, or restate it as M3 does and say what the qualification adds: agreement across repeats no longer shows the history settled the value, because the family may fix it.

findings.where: W4 section 3, bullet 4 ("M4, M6 and arm (c)")
findings.claim_in_addendum: That is the theory's own reason for M5 (ii)'s prediction that arm (c) loses what needs a target across steps, and it is quoted in phase 4's plan.
findings.finding: Read no wider than written, the sentence is about evidential independence, not about carriage. It says a derived record does not witness a history a second time; M5 (ii) predicts a loss of work that needs a represented target across steps, which is a claim about what the summary carries. A summary could carry every target M5 needs and still not be a second witness, and a second witness would not supply a missing target. What the sentence does hold for arm (c) is narrower: the summary is not independent evidence about the run the transcript recorded.
findings.evidence: File 11, Part IV: "A carrier keeps its provenance when present access to it is lost, and a later record derived from the carrier is not a second, independent witness to its history." | W3 section 4, M5: "(ii) a fresh call handed a summary differs from the stateful agent exactly on the fields whose work needs a target across steps that the summary did not carry", built on "Part IV's requirement on a constructed transport that \"\\(t\\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target\"" and Part XII's retention fixed point. | W3 section 7: "**A target** is what Part IV means: \"\\(t\\), or the organization it targets\"".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A sentence of file 11 tying a derived record's carriage of targets to its witness status would hold W4's use; I read Part IV's representation paragraph and Part IX's receipts paragraph in full and found the witness claim and the receipt claim, both evidential. If M5 (ii) were a prediction about provenance rather than about carriage, the sentence would be its reason; M5 (ii) is about fields whose work needs a target.
findings.forced_edit: Say what the sentence holds (arm (c)'s summary is not a second witness to the run, which bears on receipts and on M7), and leave M5 (ii)'s reason as the construction W3 marked on Part XII and Part IV.

findings.where: W4 section 3, bullet 3 ("M9 and the premise of the skill map")
findings.claim_in_addendum: A skill's router table is "an instruction about what to read". So ... the skill map's premise has a passage: a skill carried as text inside the boundary is the system's own today whoever wrote it, and the same skill supplied from outside is an outside contribution.
findings.finding: The quoted paragraph says the opposite of the conclusion for exactly the item W4 picks. "An instruction about what to read" is named there as work supplied from outside that "remains an outside contribution however it is executed inside"; the clause W4 borrows for the in-context case is about a process that runs inside, not about an instruction. Calling the router table an instruction about what to read therefore puts it on the outside-contribution side of the same sentence. The paragraph is about ownership of a subhistory in Build; it is not a passage that joins a carrier to an operation, which is what the skill map's premise needs.
findings.evidence: File 11, Part X, "Ownership": "Work supplied from outside that boundary, a diagnosis, a decisive question, an instruction about what to read, remains an outside contribution however it is executed inside; a process that runs inside the boundary is the system's own today whoever wrote it; and where the boundary is drawn decides, not where the process sits in the casing." | W3 section 6: "'A skill is a carrier of one or more of the theory's operations for an agent' is not in file 10, which has carriers (Part IV's occurrences) and predicates (the dependence order) and does not join them". | W3 section 4, indices: "a policy carried as text in the context is inside".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: If the list in the first clause were of things supplied from inside, or if the second clause named instructions as well as processes, W4's reading would stand; the first clause is governed by "supplied from outside that boundary" and the second by "a process that runs inside the boundary". If the declared boundary put the writing of the skill inside, the first clause would not fire; W3's boundary puts the record and the owner outside.
findings.forced_edit: Say which clause governs: under W3's boundary the skill's text in the context is inside, while the work of writing it stays an outside contribution however executed inside; and keep the skill-map premise's permitting passages as W3 named them (Part I, Part XIII), since Part X's Ownership joins no carrier to an operation.

findings.claim_in_addendum: W3's condition (no claim about construction resting on the declared frame) is this sentence applied to M1, M4 and M7.
findings.finding: Two different faults are run together. W3's condition forbids resting a construction claim on a declaration, which is Part 0's sentence and is already quoted in W3. File 11's new sentence forbids circular justification in the dependence order, and its second limb names an ownership and a capability justified only by each other, whose plainest target in the model is M5's definition of the constructor attribute. W4 applies the sentence to M1, M4 and M7 and does not ask whether M5 passes it, although it quotes the matching Part XII clause one bullet earlier and leaves M5's mark unchanged.
findings.evidence: File 11, Part XIV: "The order is well founded: a representation justified only by its own construction, or an ownership and a capability justified only by each other, has not supplied its place in it, and a separate proof that would supply it counts only when the account uses it." | File 11, Part 0: "Declaration is permitted only as a modelling convenience, and a claim about creativity cannot rest on it." (quoted in W3 section 4). | W3 section 9: "Any claim of the model about construction or creativity resting on the declared frame M1: the theory forbids resting on declaration claim by claim, not in proportion." | File 11, Part XII: "Ownership is grounded in the processes and resources the boundary includes, never in the capability being attributed". | W3 section 4, M5: "a stateful agent is one whose constructor attribute ... is the set of states carrying the represented targets of its unfinished work".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: If W3's section 9 condition were about circularity, the two would be one; its words are "resting on the declared frame M1" and "resting on declaration". On the M5 half, if the constructor attribute were fixed only by the arrangement (what the rig hands over) the circularity clause would not bite, and that reading is available; so the M5 half is a candidate, not forced, and what is forced is only that the addendum says which.
findings.forced_edit: Say that the sentence adds a second, different condition (circular justification) beside W3's declaration condition, and add one line saying whether M5's constructor attribute is fixed independently of the capability it is used to predict.

verdict:
**1. The question, frozen.** What is explained: W4's claim that the plan can be re-based on file 11 by replacing one sentence of authority, restating M2, and naming nine new holders, with nothing else changed and three things given up. Range: W4's seven sections, and W3 read with it, against file 11 sentence by sentence, with file 10 beside it where W4 compares. What is asked, four things: are W4's quotations of file 11 verbatim and at the Part named; are W3's own quotations of file 10 either verbatim in file 11 or on W4's list; is M2's new statement held by file 11's sentences read no wider than written; do the section 3 passages hold what W4 says, more, or less; is the device the record's, and does anything rest on file 11 alone that section 6 leaves unnamed. The kind of question is rule-status (does this sentence hold that claim) with a backward half (what the record's words show). Frozen throughout; nothing below changes it.

**2. The explanation in parts, and the jobs.** Parts, in W4's words: (1) "the theory this programme is written to is file 11, read beside file 10" with the "10 and 11" / "11 only" mark; (2) the restated M2 under the qualified Derivation 3; (3) the nine sentences that "hold parts W3 had marked as constructions or held if", plus the Part II sentence for the HV ask; (4) "Five, none changing a claim" and "The four other quotations file 11 no longer carries"; (5) "What does not change"; (6) "What this addendum gives up, in one list"; (7) three traps. Jobs: J1 *given* (decision W2, "Here's the updated first"): follow file 11 without editing W3 or Semantics. J2 *fixed* (Planning file 2's `freezing.md`, as W4 cites it): a change recorded before the first run that names what it gives up. J3 *given* (S6, H8): edit nothing outside this project. J4 *added* by this test: every quotation verbatim and at its Part, every claim about a document checked against the document's words. J5 *added*: what rests on file 11 alone can be found and re-derived if round S76 does not let file 11 stand.

**3. Part by part.** *Part 1, the authority sentence and the device:* **held** by S64's own words, provenance built; **held if** for its reach, because the device is declared for phase 1's word list while section 3 puts file-11-only sentences into phase 4's plan and into two asks already made to the HV project. *Part 2, the restated M2:* the population clause is **loose** (file 11's population is of transports, fixed by "the physics and the stated construction"; W4 says parameter family, and the paragraph says both); "fixed by the family where it does not" is **held** by the proof's last sentence; the two-way reading of an arm difference **contradicts** W3's own one-reader design and is held by no sentence of file 11; the mark is **held if** on a premise nothing now settles, the independence falsifier having been dropped. *Part 3, the nine holders:* six hold what W4 says and no more (boundary and continuity; ownership grounded in the boundary; the obligations as declared inputs; a mentioned dimension not a port; the theorem's assumptions; the criticality sentence). Bullet 3 (an instruction about what to read) **contradicts** the first clause of the very sentence it quotes. Bullet 4 (a later record is not a second witness) is **loose**: it is an evidential claim, not a claim about carriage, so it is not M5 (ii)'s reason. Bullet 9 (the well-founded order) **contradicts** W3's section 9 condition, which is about declaration, and leaves the clause's ownership-and-capability limb unapplied to M5. Bullet 5's P1.1 analogy is **loose** and its active-route quotation **idle**. *Part 4, the rewordings:* incomplete — Part VII's attack-(B) sentence changed and is not listed, and one phrase given as file 11's is the record's. *Part 5, what does not change:* **contradicts** itself in three places (Q2 and Q4 against W3's M2 and section 9; P1.1's file; M6's unqualified clause). *Part 6, what is given up:* **held** as far as it goes, and silent on the nine holders, on the rewrite's self-description and on the new M2's own dependence on 11. *Part 7, the traps:* **held**, and trap 1 is the sentence that keeps the whole addendum honest about its footing. Provenance: parts 1 and 4 *built* on the record and the program; part 2 *built*; part 3 *built*, two bullets *asserted* where the passage is read past its clause; parts 5 and 6 *asserted*.

**4. Whole-explanation checks.** *Flip:* had file 11 changed nothing, section 3 would have no bullets and section 2 no restatement, so those parts could not have been written either way; section 5 could have been written whatever file 11 said, and it is the part that fails three times — it is a catch-all, and its gauge is exactly the count of W3 sentences it silently leaves wrong. *Reverse:* poking file 11 moves W4 where it should (the Derivation 3 family), and fails to move it at Part VII, where inserting "in Part XV" left W4 unchanged; poking W4 moves nothing in file 11, which is the right direction. *Answer hidden in the starting points:* section 4's "none changing a claim" is checked against a program whose output shows it never read three of the quotations, so the conclusion partly restates the search. *Add a job:* asking the addendum to say what happens if file 11 does not stand is the job that ruled out most; section 6 survives it for M2 and does not for the nine holders. *Look inside:* the test cannot bite here, because nothing has run — W4 says "It is a draft until two Opus 5 judges armed with the hard-to-vary skill have read it against file 11 (log W5)", and log W4 says "Not tested: nothing run" — so whether the restated M2 does work in a run stays **unknown**, with phase 4 named as the test. *Pairs that pull:* section 5 ("nothing changes") against section 2 (M2 changes, and with it what P4.5 falsifies and what P1.1 checks); section 5 gives way, and the line is drawn in the wrong place at P1.1 and M6. Also section 1's rule (follow file 11 where the two differ *in what is claimed*) against section 4's practice (quote file 11's wording where only the wording differs): the practice is wider than the rule, and nothing says so. *Check the patches:* the addendum is itself a patch on W3, made before the first run, which is the licensed form; the patch that needs watching is "Mark unchanged", repeated ten times, which absorbs every new sentence without cost. *What the change list leaves out:* it does not cover the quotations in W3 the program mis-parsed, and does not cover uses of file 11 outside phase 1's word list. *Rivals:* the rival addendum, one that waits for round S76 and re-bases nothing until file 11 stands, is separated from this one by exactly the owner's word and by the "11 only" marks; nothing else in W4 tells the two apart, and W4 says so in section 6's third item.

**5. What would make it harder to vary.** Two things. First, a re-run of the quote check with the pairing fixed, kept with its program, so that "nine" is a count of a search that read every row; that is the single cut that would tighten sections 4 and 1 at once. Second, one line per section-3 bullet saying what the passage does *not* hold — the exercise that would have caught bullets 3, 4 and 9, where the addendum's own named fault (a passage read wider than written, found twice by H69 and twice by W2) has recurred.

**6. What this does not show.** Nothing here says file 11 is right, or that the qualified Derivation 3 is true, or that the plan will work. It says which of W4's sentences file 11's words hold and which they do not. A loose part is not a wrong one: the population clause may well be the right reading of a language model, and nothing in file 11 forbids it; it is simply not what file 11's sentences say. Nor does this test reach whether the model, once built, describes an agent: no run exists, and Derivation 9 bounds what a run could settle.

**7. One next step.** Fix the quote pairing and re-run the check against file 11 over both W3 and W4, keeping the program; then make the four edits that carry the most: add Part VII's sentence to section 4, restate M6's clause, say in section 5 that P1.1's file changes, and add the nine holders to section 6 as resting on file 11 alone.
